doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Amateur baseball in Algiers and the story of the substituted players
summary: Martin says Yank played on an amateur team whose park was in front of his house. Tom tells a story of a game against the Sweevers where the home side slipped two ringers in, with a mascot who shouted for them.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don't know him to do nothing but play music. It's just music, huh? Yeah. You talked about that ball team, that Yank, was it? That some of them played baseball?
Yeah, Yank, he was playing on.
Was that just an amateur or was it a professional club or what did they do? No, it was just amateur.
Of course they had the park, you understand? It wasn't even no professional. Where did they play?
Where was the park over there? Right in front of Yank House. Right there?
Right in the main. Is that where they played the Sweevers?

Eh? When they slipped a Fuduki in there and beat the game. That's right. I was there that time. They slipped two fellas in there, a rabbit and a Fuduki, and they slipped them and fell in there and they had them. They had them about. Yeah. Sweevers was eating them up. Yeah. The Sweevers, and they slipped them, but I don't know how they felt slipping in there. A rabbit got behind the bat and Fuduki and everything. They said, shout Fuduki, and they were shouting too. I told them they had to get fished for me. I knew how they picked him up for me after the game was over. They had a team from the country, had them going. But they slipped them two fellas in there, I don't know how they slipped. He was from the... Sweevers. Sweevers. I know what it was good, but the Padukas that was playing with them fellas out there. Yeah, from McClendonville. McClendonville. And I slipped them two fellas in there, I don't know. He was a pitcher, oh?

Paduka was a pitcher? And the rabbit was the catcher? Yeah. And how they slipped them two fellas in there, them fellas was running away with them. Yeah. But the Paduka had to slip them two fellas in there. I'd stand up there and every time they'd strike them fellas out, every time they'd go in. And he used to do that shout. All he used to say, shout Fuduki. A large mascot. A large mascot. A large mascot. A large mascot. Fuduki. And they picked him up and carried him away in the ballroom. They told him. They told him from there, well, he won the game. Them fellas were eating him up. And how they all slipped them fellas in there? I asked you that the other day. How they all slipped them two fellas in there? I don't know. How small? I was a mascot. I was a little boy a mascot. You said they took the suit off the other fella. They did.
They had to. Yeah. Put it on him at the career point.
Yeah. They took the suit off the other fellas out, I see the strings, put them two fellas in there. I said how could they do that?
You take Coach Frankie Duesen out and I don't remember he was four that time.
Joe Ivory and Flood. Flood and all of them was playing then.
Flood, what? Flood Ivory. Flood Ivory. What did he play? I don't know. He played ball. Oh, he played ball. I didn't know. I didn't know. I didn't know. It might be a musical instrument too.
